title: Glyphosate Explained: Why Organic Food is the Only Way to Avoid Roundup
summary: Explainer arguing glyphosate harms gut bacteria, soil life and weeds' susceptibility, and that certified organic food is the way to avoid it.

assertions.quote: If it is certified organic, it was grown without glyphosate.

verdicts.note: Organic foods rarely carry glyphosate residues and diet switches lower urinary levels, though drift can leave traces and residue-tested labels also exist.

Some studies also measured glyphosate (via AMPA) and organic diet interventions markedly reduced urinary levels, which supports organic as a way to cut exposure but does not compare it with other ways.

In four U.S. families (16 people), five days on an all-organic diet cut mean urinary glyphosate by about 71% and AMPA by 77%, so organic food is an effective way to cut exposure; the study, funded by an advocacy group, did not compare it with any other way, so 'most reliable' is untested.

assertions.quote: sometimes even used as a desiccant to dry out crops like oats and wheat for faster harvesting
glyphosate can act like a low-dose antibiotic, potentially killing off the good bacteria
Research has shown that glyphosate can be devastating to this underground world.
many weeds have evolved to survive it

verdicts.note: Dozens of weed species have evolved glyphosate resistance, documented widely in Roundup Ready cropping systems.

assertions.quote: it does not guarantee a product is glyphosate free
